steps.fb: Connect this URL in Zapier or Meta’s Lead Ads webhook to forward each Instant Form submission here. A native one-click Facebook login is on the way.
steps.google_ads: In Google Ads, open your Lead Form asset → Data → add a webhook. Paste the Webhook URL below and use the API key as the “Key”.
steps.website: Add this as your form’s POST action, or send a JSON POST from your site. The first submission auto-creates matching columns.
steps.webhook: Paste this endpoint into the platform. Every POST creates a lead on your board.
steps.email: Portal email import is coming soon — you’ll forward the portal’s lead emails to a unique address and we’ll parse them onto your board.
steps.poll: Google Forms sync is coming soon — connect Google and pick a form; we’ll pull new responses on a schedule.
steps.snippet: Paste this one line into your website, just before </body> on every page (or in your site builder’s footer/custom-code setting). That’s the whole setup — no other code.

body.meta: LeadLoop will stop sending events to Meta and stop pulling Lead Ads from your Pages. Your Pixel, ads and existing leads are not touched.
body.google: LeadLoop will stop uploading conversions to Google Ads and forget its access. Your conversion actions and campaigns stay as they are.
body.tiktok: LeadLoop will stop sending events to TikTok and stop pulling Instant Form leads. Your pixel and ads are not touched.

steps.title: In Tag Manager, open [[Tags]] → [[New]] → [[Custom HTML]]
steps.detail: Name it “LeadLoop”.

steps.title: Paste the tag and choose the [[All Pages]] trigger
steps.detail: Leave “Support document.write” off.

steps.title: Click [[Submit]] → [[Publish]], then come back here
steps.detail: We’ll check your site and confirm everything is firing.

steps.title: In WordPress, open [[Plugins]] → [[Add New Plugin]] → [[Upload Plugin]]
steps.detail: You need to be a WordPress administrator.

steps.title: Choose the zip file, click [[Install Now]], then [[Activate]]
steps.detail: The plugin already contains your site key. Nothing to configure.

steps.title: Come back here and check your website
steps.detail: We’ll confirm the tag is on every page.

steps.title: In Wix, open [[Settings]] → [[Custom code]]
steps.detail: It’s under “Advanced” at the bottom of the Settings page.

steps.title: Click [[+ Add Custom Code]] and paste
steps.detail: Name it “LeadLoop”. Choose **All pages** and place it in the **Head**.

steps.title: Click [[Apply]], then come back here
steps.detail: We’ll check your site and confirm everything is firing.

steps.title: In Squarespace, open [[Settings]] → [[Developer tools]] → [[Code Injection]]
steps.detail: On older sites it’s under Settings → Advanced → Code Injection.

steps.title: Paste it into the [[Header]] box
steps.detail: Code Injection applies to every page.

steps.title: Click [[Save]], then come back here
steps.detail: We’ll check your site and confirm everything is firing.

steps.title: In Webflow, open [[Site settings]] → [[Custom code]]
steps.detail: Custom code needs a paid site plan.

steps.title: Paste it into [[Head code]]
steps.detail: This adds it to every page of the site.

steps.title: Click [[Save changes]], then [[Publish]] your site
steps.detail: Come back here and we’ll check it’s firing.

steps.title: In Shopify, open [[Online Store]] → [[Themes]] → [[…]] → [[Edit code]]
steps.detail: Do this on your live theme.

steps.title: Open [[theme.liquid]] and paste just before the closing head tag
steps.detail: Search the file for “/head” to find the spot quickly.

steps.title: Click [[Save]], then come back here
steps.detail: We’ll check your store and confirm everything is firing.

steps.title: Paste it into the head of every page
steps.detail: Most site builders have a “Custom code”, “Header code” or “Tracking code” setting.

steps.title: Publish your site, then come back here
steps.detail: We’ll check your site and confirm everything is firing.
